category_title: Students who become expressionless when their intelligence is publicly mocked
minimal_context: Javier is called to the board in front of his math class to solve a problem and show his work after quizzes were collected.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Now you got to show your work. Javier, come to the board to solve a problem.

STUDENT: (Walks to the board in front of the class to solve the problem.)

TUTOR: Go ahead and write out your solution.

STUDENT: (Attempts the problem on the board, writing out the steps, but gets the wrong answer.)

TUTOR: You need to do it like you are in kindergarten, that way you make no mistakes, right? Write this 17 times. (Writes "17 times" on the board) Right, Javier?

STUDENT: (Looks at the board expressionless, completely withdrawing and silencing himself as an act of protest and disengagement.)

options.A: Provide the student with access to similar, but more socially appropriate, sensory stimulation during math class, such as a squishy, stress-relief ball.
options.B: Frame students as 'mathematicians helping scientists' and justify mundane tasks, like showing all work on the board, by comparing them to professional mathematical standards.
options.C: Reflect upon statements, create classroom climates that do not foster microaggressions, and engage in professional development for culturally responsive teaching.
options.D: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing math problems on the board, ensuring the student works quickly through the steps during the classroom session.
